operations.payload: u32 n, then per input a list of decisions: u8 0 accepted (i32 key) | 1 refused (u8 0 duplicate, 1 unknown, 2 not permitted, 3 queue full; i32 key or -1) | 2 activated (i32 key, u8 resumed) | 3 preempted (i32 key, i32 by) | 4 ended (i32 key, u8 reason 0 finished, 1 cancelled, 2 replaced, 3 released, 4 cancelled-all; i32 by or -1) | 5 cancelled-all (i32 by, u32 count); then list of live entries (i32 key, owner, band, seq, u8 status 0 pending 1 active 2 suspended, u8 started)

operations.payload: per query list<i32 x, y, index>

inputsGenerator: scripts/lockstep-fixtures.py generate (fixed constants and a 32-bit LCG; no clock, network or host randomness)
independentOracle: scripts/lockstep-fixtures.py oracle: exact Python integers for operations 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10 (the 10^5-pair sweep recomputed exactly); a recursive Python Tarjan for 6; an independent Python model of the arbitration rules for 9; Kahn on Python's heapq with CPM by definition for 11; a recursive Python behaviour-tree interpreter for 12; exact neighbour lists from the rules, Dijkstra on heapq, path validity and settle bounds for 13; a brute-force scan by (distance^2, x, y, index) for 14; optimal cost, path validity and settle order for 4
